original_test_intent: Verify that the BMC Web TEMP_BF3_Chip sensor represents the intended BF3 controller chip and that its reading, units, status, thresholds, freshness and range match the approved platform SPEC.
original_method: Verify target, BF3 adapter instance and telemetry mapping; capture the protected Web row and page context; compare all fields to the chip SPEC; optionally correlate the exact same backend resource; preserve logs and avoid configuration or thermal-control changes.
manual_activity: A platform reviewer validates that the rendered resource maps to the BF3 controller chip and confirms all fields against its chip thermal SPEC.
required_inputs: BF3 adapter/chip physical and telemetry map
Units, thresholds, range and freshness rules
safety_requirements: Do not modify BF3, ports, thresholds, cooling, power or firmware
Reject transceiver and UBB FPGA evidence
Reject stale, missing, duplicate or unmapped data
agent_execution_scope: Verify target, route and BF3 identity
Capture complete TEMP_BF3_Chip UI row and context
Compare value, units, health, thresholds, timestamp and range
engineer_actions: Approve BF3 chip mapping and SPEC
Visually confirm the rendered UI evidence
Resolve missing, stale or ambiguous telemetry

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The exact-name ipmitool read can be a backend cross-check, but the truncated fallback and TEMP_UBB_FPGA oracle neither prove Web coverage nor the BF3 chip identity.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Capture the authoritative complete Web row first; if approved, use an untruncated exact-resource backend read and prove it maps to the same BF3 chip.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: The Web/SPEC inspection and 3/3-minute estimate remain; generic clearing and unrelated UBB FPGA evidence are excluded.

modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Bind the rendered sensor to a specific BF3 adapter/controller telemetry source, then capture reading, units, health, thresholds, timestamp, freshness and chip-range result together.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Adds component identity and freshness gates.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: A plausible temperature label/value alone cannot prove the monitored silicon or applicable limit.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: On multi-BF3 systems the project must name the intended adapter instance; no instance may be inferred from row order.

project_override_considerations: Define the BF3 adapter instance, telemetry-source mapping and chip limits separately from the next transceiver case and duplicate UBB FPGA row. Backend-only substitution requires approved UI equivalence.
expected_evidence: Target/firmware/Web route, BF3 adapter identity and chip SPEC
Protected UI capture with filter/refresh context
Physical/telemetry mapping, reading, units, health, thresholds, timestamp and range result

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: Items, Web procedure and SPEC criterion consistently target the BF3 chip. Generic clearing and DeepSeek's UBB FPGA expected output are method/reference defects.

blocked_analysis.analysis: BF3 mapping, SPEC and protected UI are obtainable package inputs; mark execution BLOCKED only if the chip identity cannot be resolved after that request.

review_improvement: Separates the BF3 controller junction from its transceiver and from the duplicate UBB FPGA resource while retaining the Web/SPEC intent.
independent_technical_reasoning: A BF3 controller junction and a pluggable transceiver occupy different thermal paths and use different operational limits. The Web value is meaningful only after the adapter instance and telemetry source are proven; a backend name or plausible Celsius value cannot establish that identity.
